newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude ticks higher in sluggish session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude ticks higher in sluggish session.

text.p: U.S. domestic crude markets generated slightly weaker results for outright crudes on Friday after early NYMEX advances faded under the weight of a sharply weaker heating oil performance.
Cash markets found firmer prices for domestic grade barrels, which ended the week on stronger footing due to increased values for North Sea crude supplies.

Diplomatic fighting between Iran and members of the European Union sparked some buying interest in paper markets this morning, but the situation looks unlikely to affect Iranian crude production or industry ties to Europe.
Other news focused on a report issued today on Iraqi weapons of mass destruction from the United Nations chief arms inspector Rolf Ekeus to the Security Council.
Ekeus warned the council in a major six-month report that unaccounted for Iraqi weapons must be found, noting just one weapon posed grave danger for the region.

The report reiterated previous briefings by Ekeus that arms inspections must continue in Iraq. Before broad sanctions against Iraq can be lifted, Ekeus must give Baghdad a clean bill of health on the weapons issue.

Earlier in the day, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said he expected the oil-for-food accord to be renewed for another six months when it comes-up for review by the Security Council late next month.

Outside market news failed to excite cash traders, who said the deals done on Friday were few and far between. A well-attended industry function in Houston on Thursday evening kept many players sidelined Friday, sources said.
Traders said refiners were looking to fill ratable barrel needs, albeit at slightly firmer differentials.
While May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing lost around 5 cents to talk late Friday at $19.45-55 a barrel, the value for sweet and sour grades ticked higher.

Light Lousiana Sweet/St. James ended around a 27-31 cts discount to the marker. Midland/WTI failed to move off a deal for barrels at 28 cts under, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire sold at WTI/Cushing -$1.25.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold a shade higher at $2.25-2.30 below WTI, with Eugene Island valued at a $2.15 discount.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was sold at $170 and $1.71, firmer than late Thursday.

Wet Brent continued to climb from extremely weaker prices, selling for April 26-28 at May Brent -50 cts. Stronger North Sea prices have taken some pressure off LLS values, as well as more positive margins and CFD's, traders said.
